title: Ingress Bridge Terraform module: adaptive healthchecks and TLS rotation for internal NLB->ALB
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (ingress-bridge) that codifies a canonical pattern for internal ingress in VPC deployments: an NLB fronting internal traffic with TLS passthrough/termination options and conditional handoff to ALB for HTTP routing. The module must normalize healthcheck semantics across provider primitives, support zero-downtime TLS certificate rotation (ACM + ephemeral certs), and emit detailed telemetry hooks for Console observability. This ticket captures the design, implementation tasks, and rollout plan for the first stable iteration used by Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes clear inputs for mode = [passthrough, terminate-and-proxy] and attaches correct listeners for NLB and conditional ALB target groups
Healthchecks are normalized such that apps behind ALB and services behind NLB report consistent healthy/unhealthy transitions (configurable thresholds)
TLS rotation can be performed with no > 250ms tail latency increase and no dropped connections for existing keep-alive flows during a documented canary procedure
Module includes a migration helper that converts existing in-house ingress stacks to new resource names and preserves existing ELB target group membership
Automated acceptance tests run in CI and a small canary VPC and pass for both AWS and internal staging account
Docs and example usage in the Terraform registry + Confluence are published and linked in the PR
tasks: Write TF module scaffold with provider-agnostic variable naming and clear outputs
Implement NLB listener + TLS passthrough option and ALB target group handoff when mode=terminate-and-proxy
Create healthcheck normalization layer (aws_lb_target_group and aws_lb) with sane defaults and override knobs
Add lifecycle hooks and provisioners to trigger discovery-shutdown for draining during cert rotation
Add telemetry outputs (CloudWatch metrics, X-Ray sampling tags pointer, and Console-ready tags)
Author acceptance tests (Terratest) validating health transitions and TLS handshake behavior
Add migration helper script and a plan for renaming resources with minimal disruption
Write docs: example VPC module usage, canary runbook, rollback steps, and cost/limits note
notes: Decision: support two primary patterns rather than an infinite matrix — passthrough (NLB TCP) and terminate+proxy (NLB TLS -> ALB HTTP) cover 95% of Private use-cases
Trade-off: terminating at NLB keeps L7 routing out of the path (lower CPU on proxies) but loses path-based routing unless we hand off to an ALB; we'll support both to give customers flexibility
Kernel quirk: long-lived connections behind NLB require careful deregistration flow for target groups to avoid RSTs; we add a configurable deregistration_delay to target groups
We prefer using ACM for managed certs in hosted accounts, but provide hooks for customer KMS/HSM-backed cert retrieval in Private on-prem installs
Opportunistic: if the customer's ALB max-connections are a bottleneck, recommend enabling prefix-KV caching in the application layer (doc note)

rollout_plan: Cut v0.1.0 module in a feature branch, publish to internal registry
Smoke deploy to staging Private account 3 with synthetic traffic for 48h
Run canary in customer-sim VPC for low-traffic service (select by label: ingress-canary=true) for 72h
Gradual rollout: migrate 10% -> 30% -> 100% of target groups in non-peak windows with rollback checkpoints
Post-rollout audit: verify metrics/alerts, run canary failover tests, and validate rollback sign-off
testing_plan: Unit tests for TF module variable validation and outputs
Terratest e2e: create VPC, deploy NLB+ALB combination, run synthetic HTTP/HTTPS flows with connection keep-alive and check for zero-drop during cert rotation
Chaos test: simulate target group deregistration while clients hold connections, verify graceful close behaviour
Performance test: measure 99th percentile latency before/during/after cert rotation and ensure delta < 250ms
Cross-account test for Private on-prem: validate user-provided cert provider integration with KMS/HSM emulation
migration_steps: Inventory existing ingress stacks by tag and map to new module naming using migration helper
Create a dry-run plan that replaces resource references without applying changes and surface diffs
Apply migration for a single low-risk service and verify healthchecks and traffic continuity for 24h
Proceed with bulk migration in waves; monitor per-service telemetry and mark rollbacks if unhealthy
After successful migration, deprecate old module and publish obsoletion note
risk_mitigation: Risk: TLS handshakes during rotation may expose short-lived errors — Mitigation: stagger cert swap across NLB AZs and use double-listener approach for overlap
Risk: ALB capacity constraints under heavy burst traffic — Mitigation: implement autoscaling for ALB target groups and provide preflight capacity recommendations
Risk: Resource renaming could break monitoring dashboards — Mitigation: migration helper preserves tags and emits a mapping file for dashboard owners
Risk: Private customer HSM integration complexity — Mitigation: provide a simple shim that falls back to file-based certs with strict ops guidance for air-gapped installs
